scene_description: Light gray wood-grain desk along a wall with a power-outlet strip at its back edge. A charger block is plugged into the outlet strip at the back edge, and a whiteboard eraser stands on its end, leaning against the charger. Front is the edge away from the wall.

vlm_input.question: Given the image and the task, robot, and status context, what should the human change, if anything, to prevent or resolve problems with this interaction? Return only a JSON object containing an ordered guidance_specs array; use an empty array if no intervention is needed.
vlm_input.task_context: The robot will collect the gray felt whiteboard eraser and carry it to a nearby whiteboard tray. The black charger will stay connected in the outlet strip.
vlm_input.robot_context: The robot has one claw gripper with parallel jaws and handles one object at a time. It uses a downward approach and a low horizontal edge grasp on the eraser body. It does not balance or reorient an object before closing the jaws.

guidance_specs.target_object: gray felt whiteboard eraser standing on its short end against the charger at the back of the desk
constraints: Support the eraser by hand during relocation so it cannot tip against the charger
Keep it supported on the desk at the end of this move
guidance_specs.context: Separate the eraser from the charger and bring it toward the front pickup area.

guidance_specs.target_object: gray whiteboard eraser after its 20 cm move toward the camera
constraints: Leave the eraser flat and supported on the desk
guidance_specs.context: Tip the eraser toward the camera until it lies flat for the pickup.

review.problem: The eraser is leaning on the charger at the rear of the desk, rather than lying flat in the planned pickup area.
review.rationale: Moving the eraser separates it from the fixed charger; a controlled tip then provides the flat pickup orientation.
review.notes: Task and robot contexts are authored scenario assumptions, not observed robot logs. All three unchanged photographs were visually reviewed; only image 01 is supplied to the VLM. On 2026-10-27 the collector authorized reuse of existing numeric candidate distances as measured or deliberately staged. Legacy T001. The collector specified 20 cm toward the camera followed by an approximate 90-degree tip toward the camera. The captured X axis with counterclockwise/from_positive_axis maps an initially upright long axis toward camera-backward. REVIEW BEFORE SFT: the initial lean and captured 3D pose are not measured. Pivot [0,-0.065,-0.0125] assumes the anchor is the body midpoint, the recorded 13 cm dimension is vertical, and the 2.5 cm dimension is depth; it models rotation about the lower camera-near edge so the idealized final body contacts the desk. The quarter-turn is a collector-authorized approximation, not a measured pose correction. Tipping adds a backward center shift beyond the separate 20 cm translation.
